meta.baseUrl: https://open-api-v4.coinglass.com — all REST endpoint paths are appended to this base (e.g. https://open-api-v4.coinglass.com/api/futures/supported-coins). Every endpoint path in the docs is prefixed with /api. Empirically probed as https://open-api-v4.coinglass.com/api in this codebase's src/core/coinglass.ts (cgGet).
meta.authHeader: CG-API-KEY — HTTP request header carrying the API key (apiKey, in: header, name: CG-API-KEY per the OpenAPI securityScheme repeated in every endpoint doc). For the WebSocket API the key is instead passed as a query param: ?cg-api-key={your_api_key}.
meta.rateLimits: Rate limit is per subscribed plan (Hobbyist / Startup / Standard / Professional / Enterprise) — the docs do not publish the exact numeric per-plan ceilings and defer to https://www.coinglass.com/pricing. The actual limit is surfaced at runtime via two response headers on every call: API-KEY-MAX-LIMIT = maximum allowed requests per minute for your key, and API-KEY-USE-LIMIT = current usage count in the active window. Breaching the cap returns code/HTTP 429 "Rate limit exceeded". Robust clients should read API-KEY-MAX-LIMIT vs API-KEY-USE-LIMIT and self-throttle rather than relying on a hardcoded number.
meta.standardPlanLimits: Exact requests/min for Standard is not numerically documented in these files (governed by the live API-KEY-MAX-LIMIT header; see pricing page). The defining Standard-plan characteristic is GRANULARITY: Standard has "No Limit" on interval — i.e. full access to sub-hour candles (1m/3m/5m/15m/30m) that lower plans are gated out of. The per-plan interval-Limit table (consistent across OHLC-style endpoints like price/history and open-interest/history) is: Hobbyist >=4h, Startup >=30m, Standard No Limit, Professional No Limit, Enterprise No Limit. So sub-hour granularity effectively requires Standard or above. History depth is not stated as a single global number; per-request page size is Default 1000 / Max 1000 rows (limit param), paginate with start_time/end_time. Most ingested time-series in this codebase reach ~360 days at 4h. Tier ceiling observed empirically: only the liquidation heatmap/map family is paywalled above Standard (returns 401 "Upgrade plan"); the rest of the catalog is accessible on the Standard key.
meta.intervalEnums: Full interval enum (per OHLC endpoint OpenAPI specs, e.g. /api/futures/price/history and /api/futures/open-interest/history): 1m, 3m, 5m, 15m, 30m, 1h, 4h, 6h, 8h, 12h, 1d, 1w. Note: documented set includes 8h (and omits the sometimes-assumed 3h). Plan gating by the per-endpoint "interval Limit" row: sub-hour values (1m/3m/5m/15m/30m) require Standard+ ("No Limit"); Startup is capped at >=30m; Hobbyist is capped at >=4h (so Hobbyist effectively only 4h/6h/8h/12h/1d/1w; Startup adds 30m/1h). Some non-OHLC endpoints use a different "range" enum instead of interval — e.g. open-interest/exchange-history-chart range ∈ {1m,15m,1h,4h,12h,all}; liquidation/exchange-list range ∈ {4h,12h,24h}; options/liquidation snapshot endpoints take their own range params. Always confirm interval vs range per endpoint.

errorCodes.meaning: Successful request (success code). Returned as the string "0" in the JSON envelope's code field, alongside data (and usually msg:"success").
Missing or invalid parameters (a valid path + accepted key that just needs a required query param will return 400 — effectively a usable endpoint, not a permission failure).
Invalid or missing API key. Also returned as 401 with message "Upgrade plan" when the key is valid but the subscribed plan is too low for that endpoint (tier-locked, e.g. liquidation heatmap/map).
The requested resource does not exist (endpoint/slug not found).
The request took too long to complete (timeout).
Rate limit exceeded — back off; consult API-KEY-MAX-LIMIT / API-KEY-USE-LIMIT headers.
An unexpected error occurred on the server.

websocket.url: wss://open-ws.coinglass.com/ws-api — connect with key as query param: wss://open-ws.coinglass.com/ws-api?cg-api-key={your_api_key}
websocket.auth: API key passed in the connection URL query string (?cg-api-key={your_api_key}), NOT via the CG-API-KEY header used for REST. No separate auth handshake message after connect.
websocket.channels: Subscribe/unsubscribe by sending JSON {"method":"subscribe"|"unsubscribe","channels":[...]}. Known channels: liquidationOrders / liquidation_orders (global forced-liquidation stream, no symbol arg; side=1 long-liq, side=2 short-liq); futures_ticker@{exchange}_{symbol} (e.g. futures_ticker@Binance_BTCUSDT — snapshot: price, index_price, OI, funding_rate, next_funding_time, funding_interval_hours); futures_trades@{exchange}_{symbol}@{minVol} (e.g. futures_trades@Binance_BTCUSDT@10000 — executed trades >= minVol USD; side=1 sell, side=2 buy); spot_trades@{exchange}_{symbol}@{minVol} (same shape for spot). The futures_ticker, futures_trades, spot_trades, and liquidation_orders streams all require Standard Edition account level or above.
websocket.notes: Keepalive: send a 'ping' text message every ~20s and expect a 'pong'; the server auto-disconnects on network issues, so reconnect+resubscribe logic is required. Inbound messages have shape {"channel":"...","data":[{...}]}. Trade/liquidation timestamps (time) are epoch milliseconds; ticker uses string datetime fields (update_time, next_funding_time). Note casing inconsistency in docs: getting-started example uses channel name 'liquidationOrders' while the dedicated page uses 'liquidation_orders' — verify against live behavior.

meta.notes: Response envelope: { "code": <string>, "msg": <string, often "success">, "data": <object|array> }. code is a STRING (e.g. "0") in the JSON body even though the error-code table lists it numerically — compare loosely. Some endpoints omit msg; all return either a JSON object or array under data. Timestamps: epoch MILLISECONDS throughout (time, expire_time, start_time/end_time, WS time). OHLC numeric fields (open/high/low/close/volume_usd) are frequently returned as STRINGS — parse to number. Pagination/windowing: limit param Default 1000 / Max 1000; use start_time + end_time (ms) to page through history. interval is REQUIRED on OHLC endpoints; some endpoints use 'range' instead of 'interval' and some aggregated endpoints require an exchange_list param. Plan/usage check: official endpoint is GET /api/user/account/subscription returning {code, data:{level (e.g. "PROFESSIONAL"/"Standard"), expire_time (ms), expired (bool)}} — use this to detect current tier and expiry. PITFALL: this codebase's empirical probing (.claude/docs/CG-docs.md) found /user/account-subscription and related paths returning 404 on the Standard key — the only reliable tier signal observed in practice was the 401 "Upgrade plan" on the liquidation heatmap/map cluster; verify the subscription endpoint against your own key before depending on it. Auth differs REST vs WS (header CG-API-KEY vs query cg-api-key). Only confirmed paywall on Standard is the liquidation heatmap/map family (401); the broader catalog (~74 endpoints) is accessible. AI-agent integration is available via the CoinGlass Skills Hub (github.com/coinglass-official/coinglass-api-skills) paired with the CoinGlass MCP service. Full machine-readable doc index: https://docs.coinglass.com/llms.txt.

groups.groupNotes: All endpoints belong to the CoinGlass v4 REST API (server base URL https://open-api-v4.coinglass.com). Auth is via an API key sent in the request header "CG-API-KEY" (securityScheme sec0, apiKey in header). All paths sit under the /api/futures/ prefix and all use HTTP GET. Standard response envelope is {code, msg, data}: code "0" = success ("0" is a STRING in examples), msg "success"; data is either an array, an object keyed by exchange name, or a flat array of strings. Some example payloads omit "msg" (price-ohlc-history, exchange-list / exchange-rank). Common reusable query params across the domain: exchange/exchange_list (exchange name strings; discoverable via supported-exchanges / supported-exchange-pairs), symbol (a coin like BTC for coin-level endpoints, or a full trading pair like BTCUSDT for pair/price endpoints — note the inconsistency), interval, limit, start_time/end_time (ms epoch). Pagination only appears on coins-markets (per_page default 10, page default 1); other list endpoints return the full set with no paging. Gotchas: (1) the entire general-market group is plan-gated only at the row level — only coins-markets and coins-price-change exclude Hobbyist+Startup; everything else is on all 5 plans. (2) price-ohlc-history additionally plan-gates interval GRANULARITY (Hobbyist >=4h, Startup >=30m, Standard+ no limit) — this is a second availability axis beyond the row table. (3) Several OpenAPI blocks are stubs with empty description and no real parameter docs (supported-exchanges, delisted-exchange-and-pair, exchange-list) — params lists are genuinely empty there. (4) Field-name typos/quirks: pairs-markets uses "open_interest_volume_radio" (sic — should be 'ratio') and "oi_vol_ratio_change_percent_24h"; the instruments doc's prose JSON shows extra fields (settlement_currency, max_leverage, funding_interval, price_tick_size) that are absent from the OpenAPI code-sample, and has missing commas after quote_asset lines (doc typos). (5) The instruments page title in OpenAPI is misspelled "Suported Exchange and Pairs". (6) coins-markets / price-ohlc-history "limit"/"per_page" schemas declare default 10 in the schema even where prose says default 1000 (price history) — trust the prose: price history default 1000 / max 1000. (7) For coin-level endpoints (coins-markets, coins-price-change) the data array element key is "symbol" (a coin like BTC); for pair-level (pairs-markets) it is "instrument_id" + "exchange_name" + "symbol" (BTC/USDT formatted). (8) supported-coins data is a flat string array; supported-exchanges data is a flat string array; supported-exchange-pairs and delisted-exchange-pairs are objects keyed by exchange name → array of instrument objects.

All endpoints live under base server https://open-api-v4.coinglass.com and require the CG-API-KEY header (apiKey auth, sec0 scheme). All are GET. All return the common envelope {code:"0", msg:"success", data:...} on success; 400 returns "{}". Two distinct response shapes in this domain: (1) OHLC time-series endpoints (oi-ohlc-histroy, oi-ohlc-aggregated-history, oi-ohlc-aggregated-stablecoin-margin-history, oi-ohlc-aggregated-coin-margin-history) return data as an ARRAY of {time(ms epoch number), open/high/low/close as STRING numerals} — note OHLC numeric fields are JSON strings, not numbers; time is in ms. (2) Chart/list endpoints return either an array of objects (exchange-list) or a column-oriented object with parallel arrays time_list / price_list / data_map{exchangeName:[values]} (oi-exchange-history-chart returns data as an object; exchange-open-interest-history returns data as a one-element ARRAY wrapping that object — a structural quirk to handle). Shared params across the 4 OHLC endpoints: interval (required, enum 1m,3m,5m,15m,30m,1h,4h,6h,8h,12h,1d,1w), limit (default 1000, max 1000 — though oi-ohlc-histroy schema default is oddly "10"), start_time/end_time (ms epoch int64), unit ('usd' or 'coin'). PLAN-GATED GRANULARITY on the 4 OHLC endpoints: Hobbyist limited to interval >=4h, Startup >=30m, Standard/Professional/Enterprise No Limit — all 5 plans can call the endpoint but lower tiers cannot request fine intervals. Pagination is via limit + start_time/end_time windowing (no cursor token). Coin-vs-pair distinction: oi-ohlc-histroy uses exchange+symbol(=pair like BTCUSDT); the aggregated variants use symbol(=coin like BTC) and the margin variants add exchange_list (comma-separated). The two *-margin-history endpoints DROP the 'unit' param (margin type is implied by endpoint). Cache freq is only documented (10s) on exchange-list and exchange-history-chart; the OHLC and option endpoints state no cache line. Typo in source filename for oi-ohlc-histroy ('histroy'). exchange-open-interest-history is actually an OPTIONS open-interest endpoint (path /api/option/...) included here for OI completeness; its 'unit' is required and symbol-dependent (BTC->USD/BTC, ETH->USD/ETH) and 'range' is required (1h,4h,12h,all).

All seven endpoints belong to the CoinGlass v4 REST API (base URL https://open-api-v4.coinglass.com). Auth is via the `CG-API-KEY` HTTP header (apiKey securityScheme `sec0`), required on every call. All responses share the common envelope `{ "code": "0", "msg": "success", "data": [...] }` where code "0" indicates success; the options/futures OI-ratio example omits "msg" but otherwise follows the same shape. `data` is always a JSON array.

Path namespace: six of seven live under `/api/futures/funding-rate/*`; the outlier is options/futures OI ratio at `/api/index/option-vs-futures-oi-ratio`. All methods are GET.

OHLC endpoints (fr-ohlc-histroy, oi-weight-ohlc-history, vol-weight-ohlc-history) share the same candlestick pattern: numeric `time` in ms-epoch plus string-typed open/high/low/close. They support pagination/windowing via `limit` (default 1000, max 1000) + `start_time` + `end_time`, and require an `interval` enum (1m,3m,5m,15m,30m,1h,4h,6h,8h,12h,1d,1w). NOTE: interval granularity is plan-gated — Hobbyist limited to `>=4h`, Startup to `>=30m`, Standard/Professional/Enterprise have no interval limit. So although all three OHLC endpoints show Standard=available, finer intervals require higher plans. fr-ohlc-histroy keys off exchange+symbol (trading pair, e.g. BTCUSDT) while the oi-weight and vol-weight variants key off `symbol` as a coin (e.g. BTC) only — no exchange param.

Gotchas / quirks:
- oi-weight-ohlc-history start_time/end_time descriptions say "in seconds" but the example value 1641522717000 is clearly milliseconds (13 digits) — likely a doc typo; treat as ms like the sibling endpoints.
- vol-weight-ohlc-history's 200-response example is empty `{}` (not populated) but field shape is identical to the other two OHLC endpoints.
- Funding-rate OHLC field names use "histroy" misspelling in the slug/operationId (fr-ohlc-histroy) — that is the literal filename, not a transcription error.
- option-vs-futures-oi-ratio: OpenAPI block is a stub (empty description, empty parameters[], no documented response schema). The real ratio field names in the response example are misspelled "radio" instead of "ratio" (btc_option_vs_futures_radio / eth_option_vs_futures_radio). The example JSON in the doc is also malformed (trailing comma, unclosed array). No query params documented; appears to be a no-arg historical series.
- Plan availability split: the three OHLC endpoints + exchange-list + cumulative-exchange-list are available on ALL plans incl Hobbyist. arbitrage and option-vs-futures-oi-ratio EXCLUDE Hobbyist (Startup and up). Standard is available on all seven.
- Cache/update frequency only stated for the four non-OHLC endpoints (exchange-list 20s, arbitrage 20s, cumulative-exchange-list 1h, oi-ratio 1 day). OHLC endpoints state no cache frequency.

All 6 endpoints are GET on base URL https://open-api-v4.coinglass.com, authenticated via header CG-API-KEY (securityScheme sec0, type apiKey, in header). Common response envelope is {code, msg, data} where code "0" means success (note: code is a STRING "0", not int; net-position v1/v2 examples omit "msg" but it is present on the others). For the four ratio/history endpoints (global-account, top-account, top-position, net-position, net-position-v2) data is an ARRAY of time-series rows keyed by `time` (ms epoch); for taker-buysell-volume-exchange-list data is a single OBJECT (not array) with a nested `exchange_list` array. Shared query params across the history endpoints: exchange (required, default Binance), symbol (required, default BTCUSDT), interval (required, default 4h), limit (optional, default 1000 / max 1000), start_time, end_time (optional, ms epoch int64). interval enum is consistent: 1m,3m,5m,15m,30m,1h,4h,6h,8h,12h,1d,1w — EXCEPT net-position v1 which omits 1w from its enum (only goes to 1d). Plan-gated GRANULARITY quirk on the three L/S ratio endpoints: although all plans show "Available ✅", interval is throttled — Hobbyist limited to >=4h, Startup to >=30m, Standard/Professional/Enterprise No Limit. The two net-position endpoints (v1 and v2) are NOT available on Hobbyist (❌); both require Startup+. net-position v2 (operationId get_apifuturesv2net-positionhistory) differs from v1 in: path has /v2/ segment, exchange is "Currently available for Binance exchange only" vs v1 supporting Binance/OKX/Bybit/Hyperliquid (and v1 mislabels exchange as "Spot exchange names" despite being a futures endpoint), and v2 interval enum includes 1w. The two net-position docs have a malformed JSON example (trailing comma, unterminated array) — cosmetic doc typo only. taker-buysell-volume-exchange-list is the only endpoint using `range` (not interval) — required, enum 5m,15m,30m,1h,4h,12h,24h, default 4h — and takes a coin `symbol` (e.g. BTC) not a pair. No explicit pagination tokens; windowing is done via start_time/end_time + limit. Cache freq is only stated for taker-buysell (1s all plans) and net-position v1/v2 (Real time all plans); the three L/S ratio endpoints state no cache frequency.

Catalog of all 14 CoinGlass v4 liquidation-domain endpoints. See per-endpoint notes for quirks. Three plan tiers: all-plans (history, aggregated-history, coin-list, exchange-list), Standard+ (order), Professional+ only (all 6 heatmap models, both map endpoints, max-pain).

All five endpoints live under /api/futures/orderbook/* on host https://open-api-v4.coinglass.com, are GET, and authenticate via the CG-API-KEY header (apiKey securityScheme sec0). Standard response envelope is {code:"0", msg:"success", data:[...]}; the orderbook-heatmap endpoint additionally includes a top-level boolean 'success':true. Common query params across the depth/large-order endpoints: exchange (single exchange name; the coin-aggregated endpoint instead uses exchange_list, a comma-separated list or 'ALL') and symbol. IMPORTANT symbol semantics differ: per-pair endpoints (orderbook-history, orderbook-heatmap, large-orderbook, large-orderbook-history) take a full PAIR (BTCUSDT) resolved via 'supported-exchange-pair'; the aggregated endpoint takes a COIN/base asset (BTC) resolved via 'supported-coins'. Supported exchanges/pairs/coins are looked up via the 'supported-exchange-pair' and 'supported-coins' helper APIs. The two bid/ask-history endpoints share an interval enum (1m,3m,5m,15m,30m,1h,4h,6h,8h,12h,1d,1w) and a 'range' depth-percentage param (0.25,0.5,0.75,1,2,3,5,10, default 1), and are plan-gated on interval granularity (Hobbyist >=4h, Startup >=30m, Standard+ no limit) while being available on ALL plans. The heatmap + both large-order endpoints are Standard-and-above only (not Hobbyist/Startup). Timestamp UNITS are a recurring gotcha: query params start_time/end_time are always in MILLISECONDS, and most response 'time'/'*_time' fields are ms epoch — EXCEPT orderbook-heatmap whose response timestamps are in SECONDS (10-digit). Pagination is via limit + start_time/end_time windows (no cursor/offset); limit caps at 1000 for the bid/ask-history endpoints (OpenAPI schema 'default' fields are buggy: show 100/500/1 vs the description's stated defaults of 1000/1000/100) and at 100 for the heatmap (which is required and has per-interval history caps: 1m=3d, 5m=15d, others=150d). large-orderbook has no time/limit params at all (pure live snapshot). large-orderbook-history is v2-pathed, requires start_time/end_time/state, filters its time window on order_end_time (not start_time), and uses an order_side enum 1=Sell/2=Buy with an order_state enum documented inconsistently (1=Open,2=Filled,3=Canceled live vs an expanded 0=Not started/1=Open/2=Filled/3=Cancelled in the history example). Cache/update frequency varies: bid/ask pair-history is 5s; heatmap and both large-order endpoints are 'real time'; the coin-aggregated bid/ask-history file states no cache line.

All endpoints live on the CoinGlass v4 server https://open-api-v4.coinglass.com and require the CG-API-KEY header (apiKey, in header). Every endpoint is GET. Standard response envelope is {code, msg, data} where code "0" = success (note: code is returned as a STRING, e.g. "0"); several examples omit msg. Most endpoints return data as a flat array; two exceptions return an object: (1) /api/hyperliquid/position wraps results in data.{total_pages, current_page, list[]} for pagination; (2) /api/hyperliquid/user-position returns a single object with margin_summary/cross_margin_summary/asset_positions[]. Pagination only exists on /api/hyperliquid/position (current_page param + total_pages/current_page in response); the history endpoints paginate by time via start_time/end_time + limit. ALL timestamps are ms epoch (create_time/update_time/time). Whale endpoints filter to notional > $1M and use signed position_size (positive=long, negative=short). Two distinct "by tag" history endpoints live under /api/futures/hyperliquid/... (note the extra /futures/ segment) and are Professional+ only, updated every 15 min, sharing the same wallet_tag enum (16 tags spanning position-size tiers Shrimp..Leviathan and PnL tiers Money_Printer..Giga_Rekt). The two distribution snapshot endpoints (wallet/position-distribution and wallet/pnl-distribution) take NO parameters and are Standard+. Whale-alert, whale-position, user-position are Startup+; the per-coin /position, both wallet distributions, and the accounts L/S ratio history are Standard+. Tag enum values appear in mixed case between distribution group_name responses (lowercase, e.g. "shrimp") and the by-tag query param (Title_Case, e.g. "Shrimp"). bias_remark enum in distribution responses is documented as bearish|slightly_bearish|indecisive|bullish|very_bullish (the pnl-distribution doc reuses the same 5-value list even though its group_name tiers differ).

All endpoints share base URL https://open-api-v4.coinglass.com and auth header CG-API-KEY (apiKey in header). Every method is GET. Standard success envelope is {code:"0", msg:"success", data:[...]} — code is a STRING "0" on success. Some endpoints add top-level success:true (orderbook-heatmap, spot-coin-netflow). Response-shape deviations: spot-coin-netflow data is a single OBJECT; supported-exchange-pairs data is an OBJECT keyed by exchange name; orderbook-heatmap and footprint data are nested POSITIONAL arrays (no field names — decode by index). Single-pair endpoints take symbol = PAIR (BTCUSDT) and param `exchange`; aggregated/coin-level endpoints take symbol = COIN (BTC) and param `exchange_list` (comma-separated, sometimes supports 'ALL'). Common history params: interval, limit, start_time, end_time (ms epoch). limit default 1000/max 1000 for most; aggregated-cvd max 4500; heatmap default/max 100. Plan-gated interval granularity (interval Limit row) on price-ohlc, spot-orderbook-history, spot-aggregated-history, taker-buysell, aggregated-taker-buysell: Hobbyist >=4h, Startup >=30m, Standard+ No Limit. Pagination (per_page/page) only on coins-markets and netflow-list. Quirks to watch: several interval schema defaults are invalid literal "h1" (use "1h"); order_side meaning conflicts between live large-limit-order (1=Buy/2=Sell) and large-orderbook-history (1=Sell/2=Buy); large-orderbook/footprint descriptions mislabel spot as "futures"; heatmap and footprint timestamps are in SECONDS while everything else is ms; some taker/netflow values are JSON strings, others numbers; several response examples omit the msg field.

All 18 endpoints are GET on base server https://open-api-v4.coinglass.com, authenticated via header CG-API-KEY (securityScheme sec0, apiKey in header). Standard response envelope is {code, msg, data}: code "0" + msg "success" on OK, data is an array. CAVEAT: most Response Data examples in these pages omit the 'msg' field and show only {code,data} (basis and futures-rsi-list are the only ones showing full {code,msg,data}) — clients should treat 'msg' as optional/present-at-runtime. Two endpoint families: (1) per-pair/per-coin TIME-SERIES history endpoints (path .../indicators/<x> or .../<x>/history, or futures_spot_volume_ratio) that take exchange+symbol+interval (required) plus optional limit/start_time/end_time and indicator-specific window params, returning rows keyed by 'time' (ms epoch); (2) multi-coin SNAPSHOT 'list' endpoints (.../<x>/list) that take NO parameters and return per-symbol objects with fixed per-timeframe columns (snapshots updated every 10s). Shared time-series params: interval supports 1m,3m,5m,15m,30m,1h,4h,6h,8h,12h,1d,1w (default usually 1h, but EMA/whale-index/td default to 1d); series_type supports open/high/low/close (default close) on RSI/MA/EMA/BOLL/MACD only; window sets the indicator period; BOLL adds 'mult' (stddev mult, default 2); MACD adds fast_window/slow_window/signal_window (12/26/9). PAGINATION/LIMIT GOTCHAS: limit Default 1000 universally, but Maximum varies — RSI/MA/BOLL/MACD per-pair = 4500; EMA/ATR/TD/whale-index/basis/futures_spot_volume_ratio = 1000. PLAN AVAILABILITY: most indicator endpoints are Startup+ (Hobbyist excluded); the 'list' snapshot endpoints (RSI/MA/EMA/MACD/ATR/TD lists) are Standard+ only (Hobbyist AND Startup excluded); CGDI/CDRI and Futures Basis are available on ALL plans incl. Hobbyist (basis has plan-gated interval granularity: Hobbyist >=4h, Startup >=30m). All 18 are available on Standard (standardAvailable=true). NOTABLE QUIRKS for the typed client: (a) cgdi-index and cdri-index OpenAPI path keys contain TRAILING SPACES — must be trimmed; (b) cgdi/cdri declare ZERO parameters in OpenAPI despite being history endpoints (symbol/interval likely required at runtime but undocumented); (c) futures_spot_volume_ratio uses underscore path and a 'exchange_list' (comma-sep) param + coin-level 'symbol' (BTC not BTCUSDT), resolved via 'support-coins' not 'support-exchange-pair'; (d) exchange-discovery API name is inconsistently spelled 'support-exchange-pair' (indicators) vs 'supported-exchange-pair' (basis, whale-index); (e) many operationIds/summaries are copy-paste artifacts ('Copy of Copy of...', mismatched 'get_apifuturesindicatorsema-1' on MACD); (f) per-pair MACD time-series returns only macd_value while the multi-coin macd/list returns both macd_* and signal_* per timeframe; (g) per-pair TD returns separate td_buy_count/td_sell_count rows while td/list returns a single signed td_* (positive=buy, negative=sell); (h) whale_index_value can be negative; (i) limit/start_time/end_time are typed inconsistently (string vs integer/int64) across pages.

All 18 endpoints are CoinGlass v4 REST, GET, base https://open-api-v4.coinglass.com, auth header CG-API-KEY. Uniform envelope {"code":"0","msg":"success","data":[...]} with code as a STRING. Exceptions: etf-price-ohlc-history uses "message" not "msg"; etf-aum and several flow-history examples omit "msg". All 18 are available on every plan (Hobbyist→Enterprise) so standardAvailable=true universally. No pagination anywhere. Timestamps are ms epoch except: etf-detail last_quote/last_trade.last_updated = nanosecond epoch; option-max-pain.date = "YYMMDD" string; ETF list date sub-fields = "YYYY-MM-DD" strings. Query params: ticker (ETF symbol, default GBTC) is REQUIRED on etf-history/etf-price-ohlc-history/etf-detail and OPTIONAL (default "") on bitcoin net-assets / premium-discount / aum; ethereum net-assets and all flow-history endpoints take NO params (hype params array is literally empty); grayscale premium-history requires symbol (token, default BTC though BTC not in the supported list); option-max-pain requires symbol + exchange. The flow-history family (btc/eth/sol/xrp/hype/hk) is the same shape; sol/xrp/hype are auto-generated copies (junk operationIds, "Copy of..." summaries, etf_flows entries may omit flow_usd for zero-flow funds). Field-naming inconsistency: rendered Response Data uses timestamp/flow_usd/price_usd/etf_ticker while embedded OpenAPI Result strings show change_usd/price/close_price/ticker — trust rendered Response Data. Field typos to carry into the client: etf-detail 'ydt_change_percent' (YTD), grayscale-holding-list 'holdings_amount_change1d' (missing underscore), premium-discount 'premium_discount_details' (a percentage). etf-detail.data is an OBJECT not an array; grayscale-premium-history returns columnar parallel arrays (primary_market_price[], date_list[], secondary_market_price_list[], premium_rate_list[]) rather than row objects.

All 9 endpoints share the same server base URL https://open-api-v4.coinglass.com and use header auth via CG-API-KEY (securityScheme sec0). All responses use the standard envelope {code, msg, data} where code "0" = success (note: whale-transfer and coin-unlock-list response examples omit the "msg" field, showing only code+data, but the standard envelope still applies). The "data" payload is an array for every endpoint EXCEPT token-vesting, which returns a single object. Two distinct response shapes recur across the domain: (1) tabular row arrays (exchange-assets, exchange-balance-list, exchange-onchain-transfers, whale-transfer, coin-unlock-list, exchanges-assets-transparency) and (2) time-series "chart" objects with parallel arrays time_list[]/price_list[]/data_map{exchange:[...]} (exchange-volume-history, exchange-balance-chart). Pagination via per_page + page (default page 1) appears on exchange-assets, exchange-onchain-transfers, coin-unlock-list; per_page Max is 100 on exchange-onchain-transfers (other per_page caps not documented). Plan gating splits the domain in two: the "exchange/balance & volume" family (exchange-volume-history, exchange-assets, exchange-balance-list, exchange-balance-chart, exchange-onchain-transfers) is available on ALL plans including Hobbyist; the "alpha/intel" family (whale-transfer, coin-unlock-list, token-vesting, exchanges-assets-transparency) excludes Hobbyist (Startup and up). Standard is checkmark for all 9, so all are usable on the project's plan. Timestamp conventions are INCONSISTENT and a known gotcha: most chart/unlock fields are ms-epoch, but exchange-onchain-transfers.transaction_time and whale-transfer.block_timestamp are SECONDS-epoch. whale-transfer also returns numeric fields (amount_usd, asset_quantity) as STRINGS, and uses field names "from"/"to" (reserved-word-ish) rather than from_address/to_address used by exchange-onchain-transfers. The OpenAPI "summary" field is present on the balance/volume family but absent on the alpha/intel family (which have terse operationIds like get_apichainwhale-transfer). Several alpha endpoints (whale-transfer params, exchanges-assets-transparency) omit the "required" key on parameters — treat absent required as false/optional. exchanges-assets-transparency takes NO parameters. Note doc typos: exchange-assets header reads "Respones Data"; exchange-balance-chart symbol description duplicates the "Trading coin eg." sentence. The supported-symbol enum for exchange-balance-list and exchange-balance-chart is an ERC-20 token whitelist (BTC, ETH, USDT(ETH), and ~40 Ethereum tokens) — many majors are NOT supported here.

All 17 endpoints are CoinGlass v4 (server base https://open-api-v4.coinglass.com), GET only, auth via header CG-API-KEY (securityScheme sec0, type apiKey, in header). Common response envelope: {"code":"0","msg":"success","data":[...]}; code "0" = success, "msg" string. Two distinct data shapes appear: (1) array-of-objects (most endpoints) and (2) the "columnar/list" shape used by cryptofear-greedindex and stablecoin-marketcap-history where data is a single object holding parallel arrays data_list / price_list / time_list (indices line up positionally) — and bitcoin-rainbow-chart which returns an array of fixed-position NUMERIC ARRAYS (tuples), not objects, with the timestamp as the LAST element. Timestamp units are INCONSISTENT and must be handled per-endpoint: coinbase-premium-index, bitfinex-margin-long-short, borrow-interest-rate, ahr999 (via current/average), cryptofear time_list, stablecoin time_list use SECONDS; puell-multiple, stock-flow, pi, golden-ratio-multiplier, bitcoin-profitable-days, tow-year-ma-multiplier, tow-hundred-week-moving-avg-heatmap, altcoin-season, bitcoin-rainbow-chart use MILLISECONDS. ahr999 and bitcoin-bubble-index use a date_string field instead of an epoch (formats differ: ahr999 "YYYY/MM/DD", bubble-index "YYYY-MM-DD"). 

Parameter pattern: only the first 3 endpoints (coinbase-premium-index, bitfinex-margin-long-short, borrow-interest-rate) declare query parameters in their OpenAPI block — the other 14 declare an EMPTY/absent parameters array, so they take no documented query params (interval/limit/start_time/end_time are NOT accepted). For the parameterized endpoints: interval is required (enum 1m,3m,5m,15m,30m,1h,4h,6h,8h,12h,1d,1w) with a plan-gated granularity (Hobbyist >=4h, Startup >=30m, Standard+ no limit per the per-endpoint table); limit default/max 1000 (borrow-interest-rate doc default differs: 500); start_time/end_time are ms-epoch int64. Quirks/typos: borrow-interest-rate interval schema default is the malformed "h1" (should be 1h) and its limit default is 500 not 1000; coinbase-premium-index JSON example is missing a comma before coinbase_price and that field is absent from the embedded OpenAPI example value; tow-year-ma-multiplier and tow-hundred-week-moving-avg-heatmap examples have trailing commas after the last field (invalid JSON in the doc); altcoin-season example JSON is truncated/malformed (unclosed array). All endpoints are available on Standard EXCEPT altcoin-season-index which is gated OFF for Hobbyist (Startup+ only). Most endpoints available on every plan (Hobbyist..Enterprise). "index/macro" family: the /api/index/* path prefix covers the long-horizon BTC macro indicators; coinbase-premium-index (no /index/ prefix), bitfinex-margin-long-short (no prefix), and borrow-interest-rate (/api/borrow-interest-rate/history) are the live-frequency outliers in this group.

All 17 endpoints belong to the CoinGlass v4 "index/macro" domain. Shared characteristics: (1) Base server URL is https://open-api-v4.coinglass.com. (2) Auth via header CG-API-KEY (apiKey security scheme sec0). (3) All are HTTP GET. (4) Common response envelope: {"code":"0","data":[...]} where code "0" = success; data is an array of daily-resolution time-series objects. (5) Every data point carries a "timestamp" field in ms-epoch and (for the 16 bitcoin index endpoints) a "price" field = BTC USD price at that timestamp — only the metric-specific field(s) differ per endpoint. (6) Cadence: 16 of 17 endpoints update once per day for ALL plans; only economic-data (calendar) updates every 10 minutes. (7) Plan availability is IDENTICAL across all 17: Hobbyist=false, Startup/Standard/Professional/Enterprise=true — i.e. all are available on Standard and up, none on Hobbyist. (8) Parameters: 16 of 17 endpoints take ZERO query parameters (empty or omitted "parameters" array → no interval/range/exchange/limit knobs; you always get the full daily history back). The sole exception is economic-data which accepts start_time, end_time (both ms-epoch; range capped at 15 days before/after now) and language ('en'/'zh'). (9) These all live under the /api/index/ path prefix except economic-data which is under /api/calendar/. (10) No pagination mechanism is exposed on any of these endpoints. (11) Response Data JSON samples in the docs are truncated/malformed (unclosed arrays, trailing commas) — treat them as illustrative only. (12) economic-data data points are NOT a price time-series — they are economic calendar events with importance_level enum 1|2|3 (1=Minor up to 3=highest impact, per inline comment).

All four files are CoinGlass v4 WebSocket streaming channel references, NOT REST endpoints. None of them contains a plan-availability table (Hobbyist|Startup|Standard|Professional|Enterprise) or an "# OpenAPI definition" block, so there is no HTTP method, no "paths" object, and no "parameters" array to copy verbatim. Consequences for the typed client: (1) method is WSS/subscribe, not GET; the "path" field holds the channel name/template instead of an HTTP path. (2) Plan access is inferred ONLY from a red inline text line present in every file — "# Required Account Level: Standard Edition and Above" — which I mapped to standard=professional=enterprise=true and hobbyist=startup=false; standardAvailable=true for all four. There is no checkmark/cross table to confirm Professional/Enterprise individually, but "and Above" makes them true. (3) Subscription protocol is shared: send JSON {"method":"subscribe","channels":[<channelName>...]}. (4) Response envelope is {channel:string, data:[...]} — distinct from the REST {code,msg,data} envelope; clients should not expect code/msg here. No pagination (these are push streams). (5) Channel-name parameterization is the real "params": trade streams use "{prefix}@{exchange}_{symbol}@{minVol}" (exchange_symbol joined by underscore, minVol appended after @); futures_ticker drops the @{minVol} segment; liquidation_orders takes no exchange/symbol/minVol at all (global stream). (6) side enum is a cross-stream gotcha and is NOT consistent in meaning: in trade streams (spot & futures) 1=sell, 2=buy; in the liquidation stream 1=Long liquidation, 2=Short liquidation. (7) Timestamp formats differ: trade & liquidation streams use ms-epoch integer "time"; futures_ticker uses human-readable "YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS" strings for next_funding_time and update_time. (8) Common per-event fields across trade & liquidation streams: base_asset, exchange, price, side, symbol, time, volume_usd. (9) Every file ends with a malformed/duplicated empty "### Response Example" header (and the trade/ticker files have a stray ```text fenced channel-spec block) — documentation artifacts, not data. Cache/Update Frequency is not stated for any of these (real-time push), so cacheFreq is empty for all.
